question: Chandrayaan-3 leaves Earth’s surface by burning a huge amount of fuel. The gases released then push the rocket upwards against gravity. Which law of motion is applied here?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Newton's 3rd law of motion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Newton's 3rd law of motion states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
• This law is applied in the case of Chandrayaan-3 launching where the gases released from burning fuel exert a force on the rocket, and the rocket exerts an equal and opposite force on the gases, propelling it upwards.
 
• The reaction force of the gases being expelled downwards pushes the rocket upwards against the gravitational pull of the Earth.
 
• Newton's 3rd law of motion is fundamental in understanding the mechanics of propulsion in rocketry and other moving systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's 1st law of motion (Law of Inertia)**

 
 
• This law states that an object at rest will stay at rest, and an object in motion will stay in motion at a constant velocity unless acted upon by an external force.
 
• It explains the concept of inertia, which is the resistance of any physical object to a change in its state of motion or rest.
 
 
 
• **Newton's 2nd law of motion (Law of Acceleration)**
 
 
• This law states that the acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.
 
• The formula associated with this law is F = ma, where F is the force applied, m is the mass, and a is the acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Newton's law of gravitation**
 
 
• This law states that every point mass attracts every other point mass in the universe with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers.
 
• The formula is F = G * (m1 * m2) / r², where G is the gravitational constant, m1 and m2 are the masses, and r is the distance between the centers of the two masses.
